_comment: F5 (docs/FINAL_OPEN_ITEMS_PLAN.md): the corpus mixes two independent axes -- DSL coverage (what
model shapes the compiler must handle) and runtime coverage (a 4-way engine fan-out) -- with
nothing distinguishing them, so every tool treated an engine fan-out as N separate DSL risks.
Every corpus model (AppGen/apps + NPDevSamples) MUST have an entry here, keyed by
'NPDevSamples/canonical-demo') -- a model with no role fails the gate, no silent default.
dsl-fixture    -- exists to exercise DSL surface (parse/compile coverage, not a demo)
engine-variant -- same DSL shape, different DB engine/config; the 'true distinct bodies' count
is corpus size minus (engine-variant count - 1 per family)
repro-case     -- encodes a specific past bug or rehearses a specific runtime behavior
showcase       -- realistic app, demo/verification value (official apps + release-blocking
samples all read this way: proving real platform behavior, not DSL syntax)
canary         -- Fast Lane plan (2026-08-01): the ONE app T1's fast gate builds+boots.
query with a real WHERE); frozen -- growing it defeats the reason it is
fast. Exactly one model should carry this role: NPDevSamples/npdev-canary.
engineVariantFamiliesComment: F6 (docs/FINAL_OPEN_ITEMS_PLAN.md): a family is a group of model bodies expected to stay
byte-identical (differing only in config.json/db.definition.json engine settings). Measured
2026-07-29 via sha256 (validate-corpus.py's own contentHash): confirmed identical. Asserted, not
assumed, by check-engine-variant-families.py -- a deliberate edit to only one member now fails.
simple-user-registry-postgres is NOT in the simple-user-registry family: measured as carrying an
intentional field rename (name -> fullName, with renamedFrom) plus two new fields (notes,
department) -- a schema-evolution repro case using Postgres as the engine, not a plain engine
variant, hence its corpusRole is repro-case above, not engine-variant.
